mainTopic: רבי יהודה's views on invalid slaughter and overnight blood, intent and impurity with food not fit to eat, and the new משנה on how many blood placements bring כפרה.
overview: The גמרא first asks how רבי יהודה could give lashes for an invalid slaughter, since a ברייתא quotes him saying a חטאת slaughtered in the south brings no lashes. It answers that two תנאים report his view differently. רבי אבא then says that a plan to leave the blood overnight does not stop a later פיגול. רבא offers a proof, but the proof is rejected, and רב הונא refutes רבי אבא from a ברייתא. Two more rulings follow, each with a proof from רבא that the גמרא rejects. The first ruling is about a plan for impure people to eat the meat tomorrow. The second is about liability for eating unroasted פסח meat or unseparated תודה loaves while impure. The perek כל הפסולין then ends. A new משנה teaches how many blood placements are needed for כפרה on the outer and inner altars. The גמרא starts looking for the פסוק behind this rule, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from a teaching where רבי יהודה says there is no liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the slaughterer could be liable according to רבי יהודה, since a ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying a חטאת slaughtered in the south carries no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would he really be liable?! But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: You might think that if someone slaughtered a חטאת in the south, he is liable. So the פסוק says: 'You shall not sacrifice to ה׳ your God an ox or a sheep... any bad thing.' For a 'bad thing' you make him liable, but you do not make him liable for a חטאת he slaughtered in the south!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question begun just before this point: could the slaughterer really be liable? It then attacks that idea with a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה himself says there is no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion assumed that רבי יהודה gives lashes for slaughtering a sacrifice in a way that makes it invalid. In this ברייתא, though, רבי יהודה limits the lashes of 'כל דבר רע' to a truly 'bad thing,' meaning a blemished animal. A חטאת slaughtered in the wrong place is invalid, but it does not bring lashes. So the two reports of רבי יהודה's view seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, which must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה.
The south side of the courtyard, which is the wrong place for slaughtering a חטאת.
'Any bad thing.' These words in the פסוק are the source for lashes for sacrificing a blemished animal.
'You might think.' This word introduces a wrong assumption that the פסוק comes to reject.

phrases.english: Would he be liable?!
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One might think that a sin offering that he slaughtered in the south
he would be liable?
The verse states: "You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה וְגוֹ׳ כֹּל דָּבָר רָע״ –
phrases.english: an ox or a sheep, etc., any bad thing"
phrases.notes: The words skipped here talk about an animal with a blemish, so 'bad thing' means a blemished animal.

phrases.english: for a bad thing you hold him liable,
but you do not hold him liable
for a sin offering that he slaughtered in the south!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption from the preceding discussion that רבי יהודה gives lashes for an invalid slaughter.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, according to רבי יהודה, slaughtering a sacrifice in an invalid way brings lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה limiting 'כל דבר רע' to a blemished animal and exempting a חטאת slaughtered in the south, which contradicts that claim.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The answer: two תנאים report רבי יהודה's opinion differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים who disagree about what רבי יהודה holds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying that two different תנאים report רבי יהודה's view in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make the two sources fit together. It accepts that each source reflects a different report of רבי יהודה's position. One holds that he gives lashes for an invalid slaughter, and the other holds that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Two תנאים according to...' This means there are two different reports of one תנא's opinion.

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction is resolved by saying that two תנאים report רבי יהודה's opinion differently, not by reconciling the two sources.

phrases.english: There are two tanna'im with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים about one תנא's view (תרי תנאי אליבא ד...)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources were thought to report one single view of רבי יהודה, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two sources are two different reports of רבי יהודה's view, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees that the offering can still become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא teaches that a plan to leave the blood overnight does not prevent a later intent from making the offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: רבי יהודה agrees that he can afterward still make it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רבי אבא says that even רבי יהודה, who invalidates a slaughter done with a plan to leave the blood overnight, agrees that a later improper time-intent can still make the offering פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some wrong intentions, such as a plan to eat the offering in the wrong place, disqualify the offering in a way that blocks it from ever becoming פיגול. רבי אבא teaches that a plan to leave the blood overnight is not like those. If the כהן later does another part of the service with a plan to eat the offering after its time, the offering still becomes פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he agrees.' This means that even this Sage accepts the point.
He goes back and sets it, meaning he can afterward fix its status.
An offering made invalid by a plan to eat it or offer it after its proper time. Eating it carries the punishment of כרת.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that leaving the blood overnight is itself פיגול. It is a different kind of disqualification. רבי אבא is only saying that it does not BLOCK a later פיגול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:
And Rabbi Yehuda concedes
that he then goes back and establishes it as piggul.
phrases.notes: He means that a later step of the service done with a plan to eat it after its time still makes it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about רבי יהודה's view on a plan to leave the blood overnight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plan to leave the blood overnight does not prevent the offering from later being made פיגול.

steps.title: רבא proves the point from a plan to sprinkle the blood the next day
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that a plan to sprinkle tomorrow, which includes a plan to leave the blood overnight, still becomes פיגול once the sprinkling happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can see this is true, because פיגול before the sprinkling is nothing, and then the sprinkling comes and sets it as פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof for רבי אבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plan to sprinkle the blood tomorrow is a plan of פיגול, and it automatically includes a plan to leave the blood overnight. The פיגול does not take effect until the sprinkling, yet it does take effect. This shows that the plan to leave the blood overnight did not block the פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Know.' This word introduces a supporting proof.
The sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח, which is the main step of the sacrificial service.
'It is nothing,' meaning it has not yet taken effect.

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול takes full effect only at the זריקה. A plan to leave the blood overnight, even one that comes built into a פיגול plan, does not stop that from happening.

phrases.english: Rava says: Know that this is so,
for piggul before the sprinkling
phrases.notes: He means a plan, during the slaughter, to sprinkle the blood tomorrow. That plan already includes leaving the blood overnight.

phrases.english: is nothing,
and the sprinkling comes
and establishes it as piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבא's rule from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's rule that a plan to leave the blood overnight does not block a later פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a plan to sprinkle the blood tomorrow. It includes a plan to leave the blood overnight, yet it becomes פיגול at the sprinkling.

steps.title: One intent versus two intents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. In a normal פיגול case there is only one intent, but in רבי אבא's case there are two separate intents.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. There, it is one intent. Here, there are two intents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof from step 4 and says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the regular case, 'sprinkle tomorrow' is a single plan, and it simply takes effect when the sprinkling happens. In רבי אבא's case, the person first planned to leave the blood overnight and later had a separate פיגול intent. Since a wrong intent was already there, the second intent may not be able to make it פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the proof is rejected
Intent or plan in the person's mind during the service
There / here: the two cases being compared

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there, it is one intent,
phrases.notes: 'There' is רבא's case: a single plan to sprinkle tomorrow.

phrases.english: here, there are two intents.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is רבי אבא's case: first a plan to leave the blood overnight, then a separate time intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof given in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבא's proof is rejected. רבי אבא's ruling itself has not yet been refuted here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compares a one-intent case to a two-intent case, so it does not show what happens when an earlier wrong intent is already present.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows an overnight plan blocks later כרת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges רבי אבא from a ברייתא. If someone planned to put the blood in the wrong spot immediately, a later time intent makes it פיגול. But if he planned to do it tomorrow, a later time or place intent only disqualifies it, with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא objected to רבי אבא: If someone planned to put the blood that goes above the line below it, or the blood that goes below the line above it, and planned to do it immediately, the offering is valid. If he then also had intent for outside its place, it is disqualified, with no כרת. If his intent was for beyond its time, it is פיגול and there is כרת. If he planned to do it tomorrow, it is disqualified. If he then had intent either for beyond its time or for outside its place, it is disqualified, with no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's two halves are the key. With 'immediately,' the first plan does no harm, so a later time intent creates פיגול with כרת. With 'tomorrow,' the first plan includes leaving the blood overnight, and now even a time intent brings no כרת. That is exactly the opposite of רבי אבא, who said an overnight plan does not stop a later פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Above / below the red line on the מזבח, where different blood is placed
Immediately, on the same day
Outside its proper place: disqualifies, but no כרת
Beyond its proper time: makes the offering פיגול
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Planning to put the blood in the wrong spot does not disqualify the offering by itself, which is why 'immediately' is valid. What disqualifies in the 'tomorrow' case is the plan to leave the blood overnight.

phrases.english: Rav Huna raised an objection to Rabbi Abba:
to place those that are placed above, below,
phrases.notes: Above or below the red line that runs around the מזבח.

phrases.english: or those placed below, above;
if immediately, it is valid.
If he then had intent for outside its place, it is disqualified,
and there is no כרת for it.
If his intent was for beyond its time, it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for it.
If he planned it for tomorrow, it is disqualified.
If he then had intent, whether for beyond its time
or for outside its place, it is disqualified,
and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's proof is rejected, a direct ברייתא is brought against רבי אבא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's rule (step 3) that a plan to leave the blood overnight does not prevent a later פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that after a 'tomorrow' plan, which means leaving the blood overnight, a later time intent brings no כרת. So the overnight plan does block פיגול.

steps.title: רבי אבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a real refutation of רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a refutation of רבי אבא? It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the final result: רבי אבא's view has been disproven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רבי אבא, so his rule is rejected. The law follows the ברייתא: a plan to leave the blood overnight blocks a later intent from making the offering פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: the view is disproven

steps.whatToRemember: Once a person planned to leave the blood overnight, a later time intent does not create פיגול with כרת. The offering is only disqualified. This refutes רבי אבא.

phrases.english: Is this a refutation of Rabbi Abba?
It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבא's rule is rejected. An earlier overnight plan prevents a later פיגול.

steps.title: A plan that impure people will eat it tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רבינא בר סילא: if someone planned that impure people would eat the meat tomorrow, there is liability. The offering is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר סילא: If he planned that impure people would eat it tomorrow, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: a time intent counts even when the planned eaters are people who are not allowed to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the plan does not count, since impure people may not eat the meat anyway. רבינא בר סילא rules that it still counts as a plan to eat beyond its time. So it is פיגול, and there is כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure people, who may not eat קדשים
Tomorrow, after the allowed time
Liable, here to כרת for פיגול

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר סֵילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Sila said:
If he planned that impure people would eat it tomorrow, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר סֵילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רבי אבא's refutation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plan for impure people to eat the meat beyond its time still makes the offering פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: רבא's support: meat before זריקה
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports רבינא בר סילא. Meat is not fit to eat before the זריקה, yet a wrong intent about it still disqualifies the offering. So an intent about eating that is not allowed still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Know that this is true, because meat before the sprinkling is not fit to eat, and when one has intent about it, it becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a logical proof to support the ruling in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every time intent is made at the שחיטה, before the blood is sprinkled. At that moment no one is allowed to eat the meat. Even so, the intent works. So a plan for eating by people who are not allowed to eat also works.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it: a phrase that brings a proof
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, which permits the meat
Is not fit, not yet allowed to be eaten
Becomes disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof compares impure eaters to meat before the זריקה, which is not yet fit to eat but can still be disqualified by an intent. The next step questions whether that comparison really holds.

phrases.english: Rava said: Know that this is so,
since meat before the sprinkling is not fit to eat,
and when one has intent about it, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 8
steps.raayaObject: רבינא בר סילא's ruling that a plan for impure people to eat it tomorrow makes the offering פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: an intent works on meat that is not yet fit to eat before the זריקה, so being unfit to eat does not block the intent.

steps.title: The proof fails: normal meat becomes fit, but impure people never can eat it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. In a regular פיגול case the meat becomes fit after the זריקה. Here, impure people can never eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. There, he sprinkles the blood and the meat becomes fit to eat. Here, it never becomes fit at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof from Step 9, which tried to support רבינא בר סילא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that a wrong intent about meat counts even before the meat is fit to eat. The גמרא answers that in a regular case the meat will become fit once the blood is sprinkled. Meat can never become permitted to impure people, so an intent for them to eat it may not count at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the גמרא rejects the previous argument
He sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
Becomes fit or permitted
At all

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say רבינא בר סילא is wrong. It only says רבא's proof for him does not work.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there, he sprinkles the blood and the meat becomes fit,
phrases.notes: "There" is the regular case from Step 9. After the blood is sprinkled, the meat may be eaten.

phrases.english: here, it does not become fit at all.
phrases.notes: "Here" means impure people eating. That can never become permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from Step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבינא בר סילא's ruling itself is left standing without support.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison fails. Meat that is not yet fit will become fit after the זריקה, but eating by impure people never becomes fit.

steps.title: Unroasted פסח meat and unseparated תודה loaves still carry liability for impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reports a ruling of רב דימי בר חיננא. Eating unroasted פסח meat, or תודה loaves before the priestly portion is taken off, while impure brings liability for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said that רב דימי בר חיננא often said this: The meat of a פסח that was not roasted, and the loaves of a תודה that were not separated, bring liability for eating them while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about food that may not be eaten yet. Even so, someone who eats it while impure is still liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unroasted פסח meat and תודה loaves before תרומה is taken off are both forbidden to eat right now. Even so, the prohibition against eating קדשים while impure still applies to them. A food does not have to be ready to eat for the טומאה prohibition to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a pearl in his mouth': a teaching someone often repeated
Meat of the פסח offering, which must be eaten roasted
Was roasted
The loaves brought with a תודה offering
Were separated, meaning the priest's portion was taken off
Ritual impurity. Eating קדשים while impure brings כרת

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling teaches that the טומאה prohibition does not depend on whether the food may be eaten right now.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said,

phrases.aramaic: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי בַּר חִינָּנָא:
phrases.english: it was a pearl in the mouth of Rav Dimi bar Chinnana:
phrases.notes: It was a teaching he loved and said often.

phrases.english: the meat of a Pesach offering that was not roasted,
and the loaves of a thanks offering that were not separated –
phrases.notes: The priest's portion had not yet been taken off these loaves.

phrases.english: one is liable for them due to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב דִּימִי בַּר חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, related ruling about food that is not yet fit to eat, after the previous discussion about an intent for impure people to eat
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating unroasted פסח meat, or תודה loaves before the priestly portion is taken off, while impure brings liability for טומאה.

steps.title: רבא proves it from the אימורים of קדשים קלים
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports רב דימי's ruling from a ברייתא. The פסוק includes the אימורים of קדשים קלים in the טומאה prohibition, even though they are never eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can see this is true, because a ברייתא teaches that the words 'that are to ה׳' include the altar portions of lighter offerings for the impurity prohibition. So even though those parts are not eaten, one is liable for eating them while impure. Here too, even though the food is not fit to eat, one is liable for eating it while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב דימי בר חיננא's ruling with a ברייתא. He then compares the ברייתא's case to רב דימי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אימורים are burned on the מזבח and are never eaten, yet the פסוק still makes a person liable for eating them while impure. רבא compares the cases directly ('הכא נמי'): just as with the אימורים, food that is not fit to eat still carries liability for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so: introduces a supporting proof
To include something extra, learned from the wording of a פסוק
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
Apparently, so we see: introduces the conclusion drawn from a source
Fit to be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof rests on the אימורים: people never eat them, yet eating them while impure brings liability. The next step tests whether that case really matches רב דימי's case.

phrases.english: Rava said: Know that this is so,
as it is taught in a baraita:
"that are to the Lord" –
comes to include the altar portions of offerings of lesser holiness in the impurity prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו בְּנֵי אֲכִילָה נִינְהוּ –
phrases.english: Apparently, even though they are not fit for eating –
one is liable for them due to impurity;
here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רב דימי's case: unroasted פסח meat and unseparated תודה loaves.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו בְּנֵי אֲכִילָה נִינְהוּ –
phrases.english: even though they are not fit for eating –
one is liable for them due to impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of Step 11 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי בר חיננא's ruling that food not yet fit to eat still carries liability for eating it while impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'אשר לה׳' (ויקרא 7:20) to include the אימורים of קדשים קלים in the טומאה prohibition, even though they are never eaten

steps.title: The proof fails because אימורים are fit for the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. אימורים of קדשים קלים are fit for the מזבח, but unroasted פסח meat and unseparated תודה loaves are fit for no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. There, the altar parts of קדשים קלים are fit for the Most High. That excludes unroasted פסח meat and תודה loaves that were not separated, which are fit neither for the Most High nor for an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof from the ברייתא about אימורים. It says the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that since אימורים are never eaten, yet there is טומאה liability for them, food that is not fit to eat can still bring liability. The גמרא answers that אימורים are fit for something: they are burned on the מזבח. Unroasted פסח meat and תודה loaves before the separation are fit for nothing at all, so the proof does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: a formula that rejects the proof just given
The Most High: here, the altar, which 'consumes' the offering parts
An ordinary person, as opposed to the altar
To exclude; to set apart from
Was roasted (the פסח must be eaten roasted)
Were separated (the כהן's portion taken off the תודה loaves)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying אימורים may be eaten. They are never eaten by people. The point is only that they are fit for the מזבח, so they are fit for something.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there, the altar portions of offerings of lesser sanctity
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא רבא just brought in Step 12.

phrases.english: are fit for the Most High;
which excludes the meat of a Paschal offering that was not roasted
and the loaves of a thanks offering that were not separated —
which are fit neither for the Most High
nor for an ordinary person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from Step 12 for רב דימי's ruling in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not rule against רב דימי's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compares food fit for the מזבח with food fit for nobody. Being fit for the altar is enough to count as 'fit'.

steps.title: Second version: the proof from אימורים that are never eaten
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא's proof is that אימורים are not fit to eat, yet there is liability for eating them while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: But the אימורים are not fit, and still there is liability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's proof. Right after this, the גמרא will reject this version too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the proof is said more sharply: אימורים are never fit for a person to eat, yet the פסוק makes one liable for eating them while impure. So it should not matter that unroasted פסח meat or unseparated תודה loaves are not fit to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the discussion was passed down
Fit; suitable

phrases.english: Another version:
But the altar portions are not fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: הָא אֵימוּרִין לָא חֲזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רבא's proof from Step 12 in a different form, as a second version of the discussion.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי בר חיננא's ruling that food not yet fit to eat still brings טומאה liability.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that includes אימורים of קדשים קלים in the טומאה prohibition, even though they are never eaten.

steps.title: Second version rejected: אימורים are fit for their own purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second version too. אימורים are fit for what they are meant for, while the פסח meat and תודה loaves are not fit at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not right. These are fit for their purpose, and those are not fit at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second version of רבא's proof, using the same basic idea as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אימורים have a proper use, burning on the מזבח, so they are fit for that. Unroasted פסח meat and unseparated תודה loaves have no proper use right now. So the two cases are not alike.

keyTerms.meaning: For their matter: for their own proper purpose
At all
These / those: pointing to the two cases being compared

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the answer is the same: אימורים are fit for something (the מזבח), while unroasted פסח meat and unseparated תודה loaves are fit for nothing. So רבא's proof for רב דימי does not work.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
these are fit for their matter,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the אימורים, which are fit for burning on the מזבח.

phrases.english: and these are not fit at all.
phrases.notes: 'These' are the unroasted פסח meat and the unseparated תודה loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second version of the proof given in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the second version of the proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being unfit to eat is not the same as being unfit for any purpose. אימורים still have their purpose on the מזבח.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל הפסולין
steps.stepSummary: פרק כל הפסולין ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל הפסולין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter. Nothing is being argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is the traditional closing line of a פרק. It shows we are finishing פרק כל הפסולין and moving on to a new chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula that closes a perek
'All the disqualified': the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, All the Disqualified

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in Steps 13–15.

steps.title: How many blood placements are needed for atonement
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: בית שמאי say one placement brings כפרה for offerings on the outer altar, but a חטאת needs two. בית הלל say even a חטאת brings כפרה with one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: For all offerings whose blood goes on the outer altar, if the כהן put on only one placement, he brought atonement. For a חטאת, two placements are needed. בית הלל say: Even a חטאת with only one placement brings atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about blood placements on the outer מזבח. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings on the outer מזבח normally get more than one placement of blood. Both sides agree that for most of them, one placement is enough after the fact. They disagree only about a חטאת: בית שמאי require at least two placements, while בית הלל say one is enough after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of the משנה text
The outer altar, in the Temple courtyard
A placement of blood on the altar
He brought atonement: the offering works
Sin offering, which normally gets four placements, one on each corner

steps.confusionAlert: 'כיפר' here means the offering works after the fact. Nobody is saying a כהן should plan to do only one placement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the new פרק. Whether a placement is truly needed for כפרה will matter for what happens when the כהן has a wrong intent during a later placement.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
All offerings whose blood is placed on the outer altar,
where he placed it with one placement — he brought atonement.
And for a sin offering — two placements.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַטָּאת שֶׁנְּתָנָהּ מַתָּנָה אַחַת – כִּיפֵּר.
phrases.english: Even a sin offering that he placed with one placement — he brought atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new perek after the הדרן in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For offerings on the outer מזבח, one placement brings כפרה after the fact. For a חטאת, בית שמאי require two placements, while בית הלל accept one.

steps.title: Outer altar: what the first placement already does
steps.stepSummary: Since one placement is enough on the outer altar, the first placement decides things. If it was done properly, a bad intent on the second does not ruin the offering. If the first had an intent to eat it late, the offering is פיגול even if the second had a different bad intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if he did the first placement properly and the second with intent to eat the offering beyond its time, the offering has brought atonement. If he did the first with intent to eat beyond its time and the second with intent to eat outside its place, it is פיגול, and one who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws practical results from the rule it just taught: on the outer altar, one placement is enough. This applies to every outer-altar offering according to בית הלל, and to all of them except a חטאת according to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first placement already does the full job of כפרה, so it is the one that counts. A proper first placement means the offering is already accepted, and a bad intent on the second cannot undo that. A first placement with intent to eat beyond its time makes the offering פיגול, and a later intent to eat outside its place does not remove that status.

keyTerms.meaning: He has brought atonement; the offering worked
Intent to eat or offer it after its proper time
Intent to eat or offer it outside its proper place
An offering ruined by intent to eat it beyond its time
Being 'cut off'; a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם נָתַן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כְּתִיקְנָהּ
phrases.english: Therefore, if he placed the first placement in its proper manner
and the second with intent beyond its time, he has brought atonement.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נָתַן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה חוּץ לִזְמַנָּהּ
phrases.english: And if he placed the first with intent beyond its time
and the second with intent outside its place, it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for eating it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אִם נָתַן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כְּתִיקְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws practical results from the one-placement rule of the outer altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the outer altar the first placement decides the outcome. A proper first placement brings atonement, and a first placement with intent to eat beyond its time makes the offering פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: Inner altar: every placement is required
steps.stepSummary: For offerings whose blood goes on the inner altar, leaving out even one placement means there is no atonement. So if one placement was done with a wrong intent, the offering is invalid, but there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all offerings whose blood is placed on the inner altar, if he left out even one of the placements, it is as if he brought no atonement. Therefore, if he did all of them properly and one improperly, the offering is invalid, but there is no כרת for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the inner altar with the outer altar. On the inner altar, every placement is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every placement is needed, one bad placement counts as a missing placement, so the offering is invalid. But a wrong intent on only one of the placements does not make it פיגול with כרת. That is why the result is 'invalid' and not 'כרת'.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל
He left out, omitted
Placements of the blood
Invalid, disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: Outer altar: one placement is enough, so the first one decides. Inner altar: every placement is needed, so one bad placement makes the offering invalid, but not כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Invalid' and 'כרת' are not the same thing. On the inner altar, one bad placement makes the offering invalid, but eating it does not bring כרת.

phrases.english: All those whose blood is placed on the inner altar:
if he left out one of the placements,
it is as though he did not bring atonement.
Therefore, if he placed all of them in their proper manner
and one not in its proper manner,
phrases.notes: 'Not properly' here means with a wrong intent, like intent to eat it beyond its time.

phrases.english: it is invalid, but there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the inner altar with the outer-altar rules of the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the inner altar every placement is required. One placement with a wrong intent makes the offering invalid, without כרת.

steps.title: Source that one placement is enough on the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we know that one placement brings atonement on the outer altar, and answers from the פסוק 'וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that for offerings placed on the outer altar, if he placed the blood with one placement, he brought atonement? The פסוק says: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that gives a פסוק as the source for the משנה's rule that one placement is enough on the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the blood being 'poured' as one act and gives no number of placements. The ברייתא learns from this that a single placement is enough on the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The פסוק teaches
The outer altar in the courtyard
Shall be poured

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know, for those placed on the outer altar,
that if he placed them with one placement, he brought atonement?
The verse states: 'And the blood of your offerings shall be poured.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מִנַּיִן לַנִּיתָּנִין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's rule that one placement is enough on the outer altar.
steps.raayaObject: That one placement brings atonement on the outer altar.

steps.title: Is that פסוק really meant for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the פסוק is really teaching this, since it seems to be needed for a different teaching found in another ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this what that פסוק comes to teach? That פסוק is needed for what was taught in another ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's source. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא will quote the other ברייתא that uses the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is already used for one teaching cannot simply be used for another as well. The גמרא is claiming that 'וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ' is already taken by a different law, so the proof that one placement is enough is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it come for this purpose?
It is needed for
As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But does this verse come to teach this?!
That verse is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ' to teach that one placement is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already needed for a different teaching, so it seems it cannot also teach this.
